Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.
List revised.

2. Heard Sri Vinay Prakash Shukla, Advocate holding brief of Sri Manoj Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Virendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.
3.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Mukeem @ Viru, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 233 of 2022, under Sections 498-A, 376-D, 323, 504 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at Police Station Mainather, District Moradabad.
Mukeem @ Viru

1 4.

The FIR of the matter was lodged on 04.08.2022 by the victim herself against the applicant,
Nadeem, Chhuttan, Muradan and Riyasat alleging therein that she was married to applicant on 03.03.2020.
After the Nikah there was an illegal demand of Rs. 1 lakh by the accused persons from her and she used to be beaten and tortured.
Chhuttan the father-in-law and Nadeem her devar used to threaten her and commit rape upon her.
Chhuttan also facilitated his friend Riyasat who is of the same village to commit rape upon her and used to take money for the said act.
In the year 2021, her father-in-law Chhuttan got a talaak between them and then got her Nikah solemnized with Nadeem after which Chhuttan and Mukeem her jeth used to commit rape upon her.

Around 8 months back,
she and her husband Nadeem were sent Chandigarh by her father-in-law.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the prosecution story as narrated by the informant is totally concocted and false.
It is argued that admittedly the applicant is the first husband of the victim/first informant and after Talaak between them, she got married Nadeem the younger brother of the applicant.
It is argued that thereafter contradictions in the statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C of the first informant.
It is argued that charge sheet in the matter has been submitted against the applicant and others and as such there are no chances of tampering with evidence.

It is further argued that co-accused Chhuttan @ Chhote has been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 24.05.12023 passed in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No. 7396 of 2023 (Chhuttan Chhote Vs. State of U.P.), copy of the order has been annexed as annexure 8 of the affidavit.

sentences.text: He further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 27 of the affidavit and is in jail since 02.10.2022.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is the first husband of the victim/first informant and after Talaak between them, she got married to Nadeem the younger brother of the applicant.
Charge sheet in the matter has been submitted.
Co-accused Chhuttan @ Chhote has been granted bail.

8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

9. Let the applicant Mukeem @ Viru, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.
10.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
11. The bail application is allowed.
